## WS-4a — Gstack-collision sort (19 → effectively 0 needed)

### Discovery

`comm -12 <(ls skills/ | sort) <(ls ~/.claude/skills/ | sort)` returns **33** name-collisions on disk:

```
autoplan, browse, careful, codex, context-restore, context-save,
design-consultation, design-html, design-review, design-shotgun, devex-review,
document-generate, health, investigate, landing-report, learn, make-pdf,
office-hours, pair-agent, plan-ceo-review, plan-design-review,
plan-devex-review, plan-eng-review, plan-tune, qa, qa-only, retro, review,
scrape, setup-browser-cookies, ship, skillify
```

### Premise reset (per design-doc note: "scaffolding-ekonomi gör count cheap → focus on identity-bearing")

Examined Lintel's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "li",
  ...
}
```

**Lintel skills invoke as `/li:<name>`. Gstack skills invoke as `/<name>` (no prefix).** No runtime collision — the disk-collisions are namespaced at invocation time.

### Decision: NO RENAMES for the 33 gstack-collisions

**Rationale:**

1. **Prefix-only disambiguation is sufficient.** `/li:autoplan` ≠ `/autoplan`. Operator-context unambiguous. Plugin manifests don't conflict (each plugin loads its own skills folder).

2. **Lintel-versions are identity-bearing.** Every collision-name in Lintel has a Lintel-specific contract (cycle-phase reference, MS-CAIP voice-tier, brand-aware output). Renaming to "li-autoplan" etc. just adds noise — the `/li:` prefix already tells operator "this is Lintel's version."

3. **L-002 respected.** Each Lintel-version was designed with awareness of the role gstack's version covers; the collisions are intentional overlap on a shared role, not accidental duplication.

4. **Marketplace UX is fine.** When operator runs `/plugins list`, they see two `autoplan` entries with different `plugin:` ownership. Modern marketplace UIs differentiate by plugin name.

### Documented as principle (durable, not v3.6-specific)

**Convention going forward:** Lintel skills MAY share names with gstack, third-party plugins, or stdlib if the role is genuinely similar. `/li:` prefix handles invocation disambiguation. Document this in `LAYERS.md` next pass.

### Edge cases re-examined

| Collision | Stance | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `careful` | KEEP | Both have own carefulness-pattern. Identity preserved by prefix. |
| `health` | KEEP | Lintel: install/upstream verification. gstack: different. Distinct contracts. |
| `landing-report` | See WS-4b | Operator flagged as orphan, addressed below. |
| `setup-browser-cookies` | KEEP | Mechanical utility, low identity-cost. |
| All others | KEEP | See rationale above. |

**WS-4a outcome: 0 renames. Decision-document is the principle.**

## WS-4b — Orphan-name decisions (4 candidates, 3 renames recommended)

Operator-listed orphans: `landing-report`, `match`, `setup-brain`/`sync-brain`, `agt-tier-stamp`.

### 1. `landing-report` → KEEP

```yaml
current_name: landing-report
description: Post-ship report — what landed in a window, in engineering or customer-voice format.
frontmatter_v1_alias: null
recommendation: KEEP
rationale: |
  "Landing" is shipping-domain (landed in main). "Report" is the output type.
  Name is short + memorable. Risk of confusion with "landing-page-report"
  exists in theory but Lintel doesn't have a landing-page-report concept,
  so namespace-collision is null in practice.
operator_veto: <set to rename:foo if you prefer different name>
```

### 2. `match` → RENAME to `skill-router`

```yaml
current_name: match
description: Semantic skill router — given free-text user intent, suggests top 3 matching Lintel skills with rationale.
frontmatter_v1_alias: null
recommendation: RENAME → skill-router
rationale: |
  "match" is dangerously generic — collides semantically with grep/match/regex
  concepts. The actual contract is "semantic skill router." Renaming to
  skill-router makes intent visible from invocation.
alias_grace_period: 90 days (until 2026-08-29)
operator_veto: <set to keep or rename:foo>
```

### 3. `setup-brain` → RENAME to `gbrain-setup`

```yaml
current_name: setup-brain
description: Configure gbrain semantic-index integration — initialize config, pin worktree, register sync.
frontmatter_v1_alias: [li-setup-gbrain]
recommendation: RENAME → gbrain-setup
rationale: |
  "brain" is ambiguous (which brain?). Frontmatter already hints at gbrain
  via v1_alias. The cleaner pattern is domain-prefix-first: gbrain-setup,
  gbrain-sync (sibling). Drops the "li-" prefix since /li: invocation
  already handles plugin-namespace.

  Note: existing frontmatter v1_alias is "li-setup-gbrain" but that pattern
  (li- as on-disk prefix) is the v0.x convention we're moving away from per
  v3.6 backlog item 4.2.
alias_grace_period: 90 days (until 2026-08-29)
operator_veto: <set to keep or rename:foo>
```

### 4. `sync-brain` → RENAME to `gbrain-sync` (sibling to gbrain-setup)

```yaml
current_name: sync-brain
description: Refresh the gbrain index from the current worktree — incremental or full.
frontmatter_v1_alias: [li-sync-gbrain]
recommendation: RENAME → gbrain-sync
rationale: |
  Sibling to gbrain-setup per consistency. Same rationale as #3.
alias_grace_period: 90 days (until 2026-08-29)
operator_veto: <set to keep or rename:foo>
```

### 5. `agt-tier-stamp` → RENAME to `agent-tier-stamp`

```yaml
current_name: agt-tier-stamp
description: Stamp agents with license tier (permissive/restricted) — enforces 5-level precedence model.
frontmatter_v1_alias: [li-tier-stamp-agents]
recommendation: RENAME → agent-tier-stamp
rationale: |
  "agt" abbreviation is awkward + unnecessary. "agent" is short enough.
  Existing v1_alias "li-tier-stamp-agents" reverses word-order; new name
  keeps verb-first ordering consistent with other admin skills.
alias_grace_period: 90 days (until 2026-08-29)
operator_veto: <set to keep or rename:foo>
```
